articleTitle: A Study on Low Power Wide Area Communication Based Multi-Sensing Technology for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of ICT-based convergent technologies to address issues such as delays in the adoption of advanced technologies in the dissemination of smart agriculture projects aimed at improving productivity and reducing labor. The reasons for the delay in technology adoption include the lack of standardization for preprocessing and data multiple sensing information, as well as insufficient standardization of sensing processing information specifications and data APIs. This leads to problems in automation of environmental information collection and analysis, and in the development of big data and AI-based agricultural robot technology required for next-generation smart agriculture. To solve these problems, this paper designs an automated multi-sensing monitoring and analysis system using the LwM2M-based data processing protocol, which is the de facto standard for IoT data processing. Additionally, a server platform employing SKT LoRa technology, aimed at cost reduction, has been developed to focus on efficiency improvement through high connectivity and low operational costs. The integration of various sensors and communication technologies to develop IoT devices with user-friendly interfaces suitable for agriculture and environmental monitoring, and high data processing capabilities, is also discussed. This highlights the importance of developing and applying protocols for improving communication standards between IoT devices and platforms, and presents design plans for sensing monitoring systems for smart greenhouse automation and plant stress monitoring.

articleTitle: Impact of Inexpensive Oscillator in Wireless Sensor Node on Packet-Level Index Modulation Method under Real Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Packet-Level Index Modulation (PLIM) used in the Internet of Things (IoT) system has been proposed as a communication method that can transmit additional data bits added to the normal data transmitted in packets. PLIM has the feature of being able to increase the number of bits that can be transmitted more or less in low data rate LPWA (Low Power Wide Area) systems, while satisfying the constraints of the transmission time, called duty cycle. The additional information is allocated to the indexes of the time slot and channel to improve the transmission rate when the packet is transmitted. The demodulation performance of the indexes in PLIM depends on the accuracy of the oscillator. In particular, when time-slot indexes are used, the effect of clock drift of inexpensive oscillators that IoT wireless node equipped with is particularly noticeable. In this paper, the effect of the oscillator accuracy of the node that depends on the temperature variations occurring in realword environments is clarified through results obtained from experiments using actual equipments, and the impact on PLIM is discussed.

articleTitle: Pairing Strategy for using Multiple Channels in Minimal Cell of 6TiSCH Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) is a Medium Access Control (MAC) technology defined in the IEEE 802.15.4e standard. In IPv6 over the TSCH mode of IEEE 802.15.4e (6TiSCH) networks, the minimal cell for exchanging control packets operates on a single channel, leading to increased node synchronization time and inefficient network topology formation as the network scales up. So, we propose a pairing strategy, which enables the use of multiple channels in the minimal cell. We evaluated the pairing strategy in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6TiSCH$</tex> simulator. In congested scenarios, it constructs a more efficient topology compared to traditional 6TiSCH and Time-Variant RGB Mode (TRGB).

articleTitle: Indoor Positioning using BLE Beacons and User Equipments in Factory Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: For indoor position estimation where global navigation satellite system (GNSS) cannot be used, methods using received signal strength indicator (RSSI) from bluetooth low energy (BLE) beacons have been considered. However, in factory environments where there are many metallic objects, the positioning accuracy may deteriorate significantly due to radio wave reflection and diffraction. Therefore, it is necessary to install a large number of line-of-sight (LOS) beacons in the environment and select LOS beacons for positioning. This paper proposes a method to select beacons based on RSSI variance in addition on RSSI from beacons. By selecting beacons with consideration of the variance, it is possible to exclude non line-of-sight (NLOS) beacons. Experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the average positioning error by 0.119[m] compared to the conventional method that considers only the RSSI. In addition, it is time-consuming and costly to install many beacons whose locations are known in the environment. Therefore, this paper also proposes a positioning method using user equipments (UEs) that are not required to be prior installation in the environment. The experimental results show that the proposed method reduces the average positioning error by 0.362[m] compared to the conventional method that uses only beacons.

articleTitle: Performance and Inference Time Tradeoff for RNN Model based Wideband Inter-radar Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: With recent advancements in autonomous driving, there has been growing interest in using CS (Chirp Sequence) radar for precise sensing. Unlike other in-vehicle sensing techniques, CS radar offers cost-effectiveness, compactness, and greater resilience to environmental influences. However, the widespread adoption of CS radar may lead to radar-to-radar interference, causing issues like target non-detection and false detection. To tackle this challenge, a method utilizing RNN (Recurrent Neural Networks) for interference mitigation has been proposed. This study specifically investigates VanillaRNN and biLSTM models based wideband interference mitigation methods and explores their tradeoff between mitigation performance and inference time.

articleTitle: Chirp-based Frequency Shift Keying for Underwater Acoustic Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In underwater acoustic channels, communication environments are generally poor due to multipath with long delays and Doppler. Since communication signals suffer from intersymbol interference (ISI), frequency-selective fading, and short correlation time, the communication performances degrade. This paper proposes a chirp-based frequency shift keying (C-FSK) and multipath combining scheme. The proposed C-FSK replaces the tone basis of the conventional FSK with the chirp signal, which aims to overcome the underwater acoustic channels. Computer simulations demonstrate that the proposed C-FSK improves BER performances by 6 dB of signal-to-noise power ratio compared to the conventional FSK.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Sink Node Positioning for Lifetime Extension of Multihop Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Each sensor node in the multi-hop wireless sensor network participates in the data relay. In the existing sensor network, nodes near the sink nodes shorten their network lifetime due to energy hole problems cause by frequent data relays. To solve this problem, we propose a ring-based routing simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (RBR-SWIPT) technique which fuses a RBR algorithm with an energy harvesting technique. However, existing studies only assume which sensor nodes are uniformly distributed, otherwise we have confirmed the performance degradation. We also confirm that the lifetime of the network changes depending on the distribution of sensor nodes. In this paper, we propose an optimal sink node location search using density-based spatial clustering with noise (DBSCAN), which is a density-based clustering, and verify its performance. We also prove that it is possible to search for the optimal sink node location according to the distribution of sensor nodes through the proposed method.

articleTitle: Generative AI for the Maritime Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Generative AI is a new and rapidly developing field of artificial intelligence that focuses on creating new data or content. Although the concept of generating content was invented long back, the latest breakthroughs in neural network architectures have made it possible to implement this concept at a much faster pace. With the availability of vast amounts of data and computational power, it has become increasingly feasible. Generative models aim to generate new data resembling the training data distribution by learning its underlying patterns. They capture the inherent complexity of the data to produce outputs similar to the training examples. Discriminative models, on the other hand, focus on learning boundaries between different classes or categories within the data. The maritime industry is a major contributor to the global economy, but it is also a high-risk industry, as it is exposed to a variety of hazards. Generative AI can be used to improve maritime safety and efficiency in several ways. Although the maritime industry is still in the early stages of adopting generative AI, the potential benefits are significant. The integration of generative AI into maritime operations plays an increasingly important role in the maritime industry. In this view, this paper discusses generative AI, its technology, various applications, and key challenges and research prospectives.

articleTitle: A Blockchain System for MUM - T in Tactical Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a blockchain system for manned-unmanned teaming (MUM- T) in tactical networks. Stable networks are required to achieve the benefits offered by blockchain technology, such as decentralization, traceability, integrity, and security. Tactical networks for MUM - T are inherently highly dynamic because they must support battlefield operations. Therefore, a blockchain system should consider the characteristics of tactical networks. The proposed blockchain system maintains multiple blockchains, integrating all blockchains into one joint block periodically. Thus, blockchain fork probability is significantly reduced compared with conventional systems with a single blockchain.

articleTitle: Blind Detection of Channel Coding and Interleaving Using Convolutional Neural Networks in Tactical Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper proposes two Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for classifying types of channel codings and interleavings blindly in military communications. In tactical communications, eavesdropping of enemy's signal requires blind recognition of the channel coding and interleaving methods. In this study, we introduce a channel coding estimation CNN model that classifies between two widely used convolutional error correction codes and one Reed-Solomon error correction code in military communications. Additionally, our interleaver classifier distinguishes between data processed with block interleavers and data without interleaving. The performance of the proposed CNN models is evaluated through computer simulations and compared with well-known CNN models, VGG and ResNet. The proposed models demonstrate comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters, highlighting their potential for efficient implementation in military communication systems.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Integrated Resonant Dual Active Bridge Converter with Seamless Mode Transition over a Wide Load Range
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, Integrated Resonant DAB converter is proposed to utilize the characteristics of LLC Resonant Converter and DAB Converter depending on the load condition. Bidirectional switches that allow seamless mode transition is proposed by deriving the point where the operation trajectories of the two converters overlap and the conditions that ensure the efficiency of each converter. The proposed converter is verified using Hardware In the Loop simulation, achieving an efficiency of over 94% at full load.

articleTitle: Beamforming Vector Optimization Algorithm in RIS-Based Non-Terrestrial Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The high frequency in the THz band is attracting attention as a key element of the 6G system because of its wide bandwidth and high transmission rate, but technology is needed to compensate for this due to the large path loss. Therefore, we introduce an algorithm to improve security performance by using non-terrestrial network (NTN) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The proposed algorithm is largely composed of two parts. It is divided into the part that optimizes the base station beamforming vector using the successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithm and the part that optimizes the RIS beamforming vector using the minorization-maximization (MM) algorithm. As a result of performance analysis through simulation, the superiority of the proposed algorithm was confirmed in terms of system security performance.

articleTitle: Experimental5G-NR-V2X Evaluation in a Real-Life Highway and Proving Ground Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This article details the experimental 5G-NR-V2X evaluation in a real-life highway and proving ground. We propose a system capable of evaluating and validating the effectiveness of autonomous driving services. This evaluation is conducted in an actual road test setting using OBU and RSU for 5G-NR-V2X communication, which requires a minimum level of 4 (level 4 or higher), an extremely high speed (150Mbps or more), minimal delay (3ms or less), and a high level of reliability (99.99 percent) to ensure robust communication even in malicious scenarios. The present study introduces the 5G-NR-V2X communication system and its experimental assessment, which are expected to contribute to the advancement of V2X communication technologies characterized by exceptional speed, minimal latency, and strong reliability. Furthermore, it is anticipated that the utilization of the recommended performance analysis technique will augment technical competitiveness within the road, transportation, logistics, and commerce sectors through the validation of services and the testing of case scenarios.

articleTitle: Semantic Communications - A Comprehensive Survey for Future Research Issues
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Semantic communication, aimed at conveying data meaning, emerges as a promising approach within information theory to address the limitations of current communication systems. This paper outlines the architecture of semantic communication, focusing on recent trends in semantic source and channel coding, as well as resource allocation. We specifically investigate recent deep learning (DL)-based semantic communication methodologies, including end-to-end (E2E) autoencoder models and Transformer-based structures, and discuss semantic coding with various data types such as text, image, speech, and multimodal data. Additionally, we analyze adaptive channel coding and strategies for resource allocation techniques from the perspective of semantic efficiency in resource-limited networks. The paper aims to propose future research directions by illustrating how semantic communication effectively overcomes challenges in resource-limited environments while enhancing the efficiency and reliability of communication systems.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Based UAV Handover Algorithm in Cellular Networks: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: UAVs execute handovers for stable communication while moving in the air. Conventional handover algorithms designed for ground users in cellular networks are not suitable as it can induce ping-pong handover on UAVs. Furthermore, the increase of altitude and speed of UAVs leads to handover failures. To address these issues for improving signal quality, research is underway. This paper discusses research trends on utilizing reinforcement learning in cellular networks to enhance UAV s handover performance. It proposes three handover methods using Deep Reinforcement Learning and Q-learning, respectively, and validates the reduction of hand over ratio by adjusting the weight co in each approach.

articleTitle: Structured Feature-Based Component Architecture Design from a Traceability Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Embedded software requires high reliability and safety. From the perspective of embedded software development, a component-based architecture promotes software reusability. To enhance the reliability, safety, and reusability of embedded software, tracking of components is crucial. In this study, we analyze the component-based software architecture design process, based on existing structured features, from the perspective of requirement traceability. We express the design method through a meta-model and conduct analysis by tracking the outputs at each stage of the process.

articleTitle: Integrated Optimization Algorithm for Secrecy Rate Improvement in UAV-RIS enabled System
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles(UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have recently received considerable research attention in the fields of 5G and 6G wireless commumication owing to their high flexibility and low hardware costs. Therefore, we introduce a penalty-based successive convex approximation algorithm and a minorization-maximization algorithm to optimize the transmission beamforming vector, RIS beamforming vector, and VAV-RIS trajectory with the aim of improving the physical layer security performance of wireless communication systems using VA Vs and RISs. As a result of performance analysis through simulation, the superiority of the proposed algorithm was confirmed in terms of system security performance.

articleTitle: Moving Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: A Promising Frontier for 6G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) have emerged as a cost-effective solution to enhance wireless communication systems. This paper explores the potential of moving RISs in future 6G communications. After providing an overview of ongoing standardization efforts related to RIS, we present the system description of the proposed moving RIS-aided communication network and introduce a novel communication scheme tailored for millimeter-wave (mmWave) high-speed train (HST) communications. Through simulations, we demonstrate the significant advantages of incorporating moving RISs into HST communication networks. In conclusion, we summarize the key findings and suggest future research directions to optimize moving RIS systems, shedding light on the promising frontier of moving RIS and its potential to revolutionize future wireless communications.

articleTitle: Towards Robust Communication in ITS: A Comprehensive Study of Blockchain for V2I
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: V2X in connected autonomous vehicles (CAV) plays an important role in information sharing through communication. The integration of V2X and blockchain has the potential to create functionalities such as seamless V2X information sharing, similar to Bitcoin, and post-accident investigation utilities that leverage data immutability. However, the integration of blockchain into V2X communication requires addressing CAV mobility. In this study, we propose a framework that takes into account the high mobility of CAVs. Furthermore, we propose a method that not only addresses this challenge but also achieves load balancing by facilitating cooperation among nodes responsible for member management. In this paper, we integrate the ITS simulator, the communication simulator, and the blockchain simulator to build an infrastructure that can be evaluated end-to-end. Using the integrated simulator, we perform an evaluation based on metrics such as latency and member change rate in a mobile environment with a single roadside unit (RSU). In the future, we plan to implement the proposed methodology and perform evaluations in environments with multiple RSUs.

articleTitle: Design of Facial Convolutional Mesh Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In various computer vision tasks such as 3D facial reconstruction and retargeting, 3D representation poses a significant challenge. Traditional models learn linear subspaces, such as Principal Component Analysis, but they are limited in their ability to represent data beyond the input. With the advancement of deep learning, the Convolutional Mesh Autoencoder (CoMA) overcame these limitations by employing mesh simplification through Quadratic Error Metric (QEM) and utilizing the Chebyshev Network (ChebNet). However, mesh simplification based on QEM can damage feature points. In this paper, we propose Facial CoMA, which improves upon this issue by using mesh simplification through feature points and Feature Edge Quadric (FEQ).

articleTitle: DNN-Based Relative Positioning Technique Using RF Ranging
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper proposes an artificial intelligence-based relative positioning technique that utilizes only distance information in unmanned swarm robotics systems. The proposed method does not require any additional information besides the distance between nodes for positioning. Moreover, it enables accurate relative positioning among swarm nodes even in environments without fixed anchor nodes. The performance of the proposed technique is verified through computer simulation and field experiments using commercial UWB modules. The proposed method outperforms conventional grid-based positioning methods in simulated experiments. Additionally, the field experiments also show that the proposed positioning technology functions well, verifying the practicality of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based NOMA in LEO Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA), which is one of the technologies attracting attention due to its high frequency efficiency in wireless communication systems, the decoding order is considered a crucial factor influencing system performance. However, finding the optimal decoding order becomes challenging when there is wide service coverage and multiple users due to the increased computational complexity involved in the process. In this paper, we propose a machine learning (ML)-based NOMA in low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems. Our proposed scheme aims to utilize ML to determine the optimal decoding order that satisfies the target signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints with low computational complexity, particularly in systems where the satellite utilizes beamforming vector and NOMA to serve each user. The numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme achieves performance comparable to that of the optimal scheme for obtaining the optimal decoding order by using the iterative calculation.

articleTitle: Contents Scene Extraction Based on Distance Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper shows the solution for automatic scene extraction from video footages. The purpose of this paper is development of automatic and semi-automatic video editing technology. This scene extraction algorithm has three staged cascade process. The first stage is scene analytic feature extraction using content deep network encoding information. The second stage is using temporal network for video feature extraction. And the last stage is clip video feature generation by maximum activation of convolution and normalization. A deep learning network is adapted for mixture with scene analysis feature and video feature information. This module showed 0.57 F1 score.

articleTitle: Hybrid Random Routing Protocol to Enhance the Performance of Routing Protocol in Source Location Privacy Using Ant Colony Optimization and Random Walk
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are networks of hundreds of sensor networks that are connected wirelessly. Often they are deployed in areas that are unreachable to humans. Their power source primarily consists of small batteries. One of the primary purposes of WSNs is to collect data from a location and send it to the base station. However, the information's location and sensitivity make it a critical safety task. Hence, WSN must take strong measures to protect the information and its location from outside adversarial attacks. The networks are also susceptible to passive adversaries' analytical assaults. Under adversarial analysis attacks, the adversary collects information from the network using traffic analysis. By this, they can access private information like sensor node locations, such as those that monitor endangered animals. The adversary can use the inforrnation to locate the animal's exact location, leaving it vulnerable to poaching by poachers. Therefore, to prevent this, the privacy of the source location is necessary. Source Location Privacy (SLP) provides security for such operations. Several techniques, such as ring routing, flooding, randomwalk are used to provide SLP for WSNs. In this paper, we propose a novel Hybrid technique that combines fake packages and randomness to enhance the SLP of WSNs. The proposed method utilizes a random walk-based algorithm for sending the real data packet to the sink and an Ant Colony optimization-based approach for sending the false packet. Our proposed hybrid routing protocol delivers communication and privacy efficiency. The privacy protection performance of the proposed Hybrid protocol is measured using the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), Safety Period (SP), and Capture Ratio (CR).

articleTitle: Enhancing V2X Communication: Machine Learning Assisted Dynamic mmWave Beam Search
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges of dynamic beam search in millimeter wave (mmWave) communications for vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications. With the rapid mobility of connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) and dense urban environments, maintaining high-quality mmWave con-nections is critical for the reliability and efficiency of V2X communications. We propose a novel machine learning-assisted framework for dynamic mmWave beam search, which signif-icantly enhances the adaptability and performance of V2X communication systems. Our approach leverages real-time environmental data and CAV dynamics to predict optimal beam directions, improving connection stability. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in a real-world road scenario, offering a partial improvement over conventional beam search techniques.

articleTitle: Towards Data Quality Standardization for Electricity AMI Data Platform in Housing
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: As the demand for power energy rises, managing energy data quality effectively is becoming increasingly important. However, ensuring high-quality data remains challenging due to various factors such as errors in data entry, inconsistencies, and missing values. This paper highlights the need for data quality standardization to optimize the electricity Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) data platform. Specifically, it focuses on improving the quality of AMI data in housing, discussing crucial strategies for standardizing data quality, and proposing an approach to address issues that directly affect AMI data's accuracy, reliability, and usability. Therefore, this paper emphasizes the importance of standardization in enhancing the efficiency and data-driven optimization of the electricity AMI data platform, thus improving the energy data quality in the electricity AMI big data platform in housing.

articleTitle: Design of an ECG Stream Analysis Framework Based on FHIR Data Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper designs an ECG stream analysis framework based on the FHIR model, integrating Google Cloud services, including Healthcare APIs. Its aim is to provide an efficient cooperation environment for medical groups, fully exploiting the standardization of complex medical records. After the resource storage is created in the cloud and an external access interface is installed on a remote PC, an application can access the ECG stream resource stored in the cloud, promisingly combining diverse data analysis and artificial intelligence utilities. Most data-centric interactions are executed via the commonly used web interface, supporting CRUD operations. The FHIR standard makes it possible to locate the exact resource in the complex web request and response messages that embed multiple descriptive resources.

articleTitle: A method for estimating local 5G time division duplex patterns using spectrum sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Local 5G, which enables autonomous deployment of cellular communication services independent of mobile operators, has attracted much attention. When multiple Local 5G base stations deploy their services at the same time, there is a significant degradation of communication performance due to interference in the same frequency between systems. Therefore, the time for base stations and terminals to access the same frequency interference is different. Therefore, it is effective to identify whether the interference source at each time is a base station or a terminal in order to countermeasure same-frequency interference. However, information on the TDD schedule, which is the switching pattern between uplink and downlink of other Local 5G TDDs in an autonomous system, may not be available. Therefore, in this study, we established a method to estimate the TDD schedule by power detection. By controlling the tilt angle of the antenna deployed at the base station, it is possible to improve the accuracy of discriminating between terminal emissions during the uplink and base station emissions during the downlink. The TDD frame discrimination accuracy of the proposed method was clarified through actual experiments in the millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: Enhancing Data Rate of Asynchronous Pulse Code Multiple Access for Massive IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Asynchronous Pulse Code Multiple Access (APCMA) has been proposed as a wireless communication system suitable for Massive IoT, which is resilient against high-volume packet transmissions from numerous devices. Previous studies have demonstrated its effectiveness compared to other Low Power Wide Area (LPWA) protocols by experimentally evaluating it in the 920 MHz band. Chirp Spread Spectrum-based (CSS)-APCMA has also been proposed to enhance the reception sensitivity of APCMA, enabling long-range communication similar to other LPWA systems. In this paper, we evaluate the throughput performance of optimized CSS-APCMA with enhanced time resolution and broader bandwidth. We have implemented the proposed CSS-APCMA using USRP and GNU Radio and conducted experiments to explore the maximum achievable throughput and evaluate its performance in high-density wireless environments. Our experimental results demonstrate a significantly higher throughput compared to conventional APCMA.

Author Keywords: Massive Internet of Things (Massive Io T)

articleTitle: Fast Personalized PageRank for Customized Analysis Range Using Static Index
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: PPR is an essential computation for customized graph analysis, and its fast computation methods have been proposed. FORA +, one of the fastest methods, introduces an index to speed up PPR computation by referencing the end nodes of pre-generated random walks with a specific termination probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{index}$</tex>. Although for customized graph analysis, it is essential to query with different termination probabilities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> for controlling the analysis range, FORA + does not contribute to the speedup for such different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> other than the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{index}$</tex>. This paper proposes a method to quickly determine the end nodes of random walks for arbitrary termination probabilities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha (\leq\alpha_{index})$</tex> by focusing on the fact that the random walks become probabilistically longer as the termination probability decreases. In particular, we repeatedly reference the index based on the probability <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> defined by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha_{index}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> to make the longer random walks. By defining <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$p$</tex> according to mathematical considerations, the results of our method are guaranteed. In addition, our method can be used in FORA + without modifying its index structure. We incorporate our method into FORA + and evaluate the processing time using six real-world graph datasets. As a result, our method achieves up to 19.8 times speedup over the existing index-free method.

articleTitle: A Study on Automotive Data Compression Technology On-Device Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Research on autonomous driving cooperation has been extensively studied. However, sensor reliability and negotiation errors are expected in the cooperation process. Thus, it is necessary to compress and store historical data and sed it to a cloud platform for analysis. However, an efficient compression method is required to transmit historical data from the device. In this research, we study on technologies for analyzing vehicle data and compressing vehicle data on the device.

articleTitle: A Real-time Design of Stereo Vision System using Disparity Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time stereo vision system to extract disparity map with good error rate from stereo images. The error rate was reduced by the disparity calibration module that can correct errors in the initial disparity map using adaptive support-weights. Performance can be improved by overlapping the initial disparity and the disparity calibration stages. Because the adaptive support-weight algorithm includes nonlinear functions, it is impossible to reuse already processed data. In this study, we designed the system to reuse data by separating rows and columns, and as a result, performance is improved so that real-time processing is possible. To optimize the delay path, the exponential function is approximated with a step function and five stage pipeline is applied to the division operation. The proposed architecture was designed using VerilogHDL and synthesized with DBhitek 110nm standard cell library. The synthesized system used 33K gates and 4.9KB memory and showed a maximum frequency of 666MHz (57fps) and error rate of 1.88% for tsukuba image.

articleTitle: A Data-Gathering Underwater Medium Access Control Scheme Using Carrier Sensing Associated Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a medium access control method in underwater sensor networks aimed at gathering data from multiple sensor nodes to a sink node. Considering the long propagation delay of underwater acoustic channels, exchanging control packets between nodes is inefficient. In our work, sensor nodes are trained through a machine learning and determine the correct timing for data transmission to avoid possible collisions without exchanging control packets. To learn varying channel conditions, sensor nodes employ a carrier sensing. Simulation results reveal that among machine learning models, the proposed scheme utilizing the MLP model exhibits the most outstanding performance.

articleTitle: Fast prototyping of Quantized neural networks on an FPGA edge computing device with Brevitas and FINN
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a solution for fast proto-typing of Deep learning neural network models on edge computing devices like FPGA for researchers with limited knowledge of high level languages like VHDL. We use Xilinx’ Brevitas tool for Quantization and FINN framework for deployment/inference on Pynq-Z2 board. The paper will also share presently available methods for FPGA prototyping and how tools like Brevitas and FINN can be used for more efficient inference of DNN on small scale edge computers like FPGA by levaraging their 1. Quantization Aware Training(QAT) and Post Training Quanti-zation(PTQ) 2. Streamlining networks and transformations 3. Dataflow partitioning of the NN model using FINN compiler 4. DMA, FIFO and IP generation for HW build and 5. Inference on FPGA using PYNQ python Driver. The weights and activations of a custom model were quantised from floating points to 8, 4 and 2 bit for which an accuracy drop of 0.1 %, 0.8% and 7.6% was observed respectively.

articleTitle: A Study on Universal Digital Wallet for Web 3*
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The demand for self-sovereign identity/data is being secured with the emergence of blockchain, encryption technology, and cryptocurrency, and a Web 3.0 ecosystem that enables de-centralized economic activities is being discussed. Digital wallets will play an essential role in the Web 3.0 ecosystem, with the ability to make fiat- and cryptocurrency-based payments, store identity and credentials, and store one's sensitive data. In this paper, we examine the characteristics of Web 3.0, investigate and analyze the pros and cons of digital wallets, and discuss common functional requirements for different types of digital wallets. Finally, we summarize research trends of organizations related to universal digital wallets.

articleTitle: Implementation of Multifaceted Safety Indicators-Based Battery Protection System for Battery Faults and Failures
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In the realm of energy storage systems (ESS), the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries introduces significant safety challenges. In this paper, we propose a battery protection system (BPS) based on multifaceted safety indicators (MSI) to address these safety challenges. The MSI-based BPS enhances stable ESS operations by harnessing fundamental, domain-specific, and AI-based MSI modules for lithium-ion battery safety. The MSI-based BPS enables real-time monitoring and tracking on the edge cloud infrastructure without modification of functionalities in existing battery management systems (BMS). As a result of the demonstration conducted on the ESS testbed, we have validated the MSI-based BPS's effectiveness in preemptively identifying and mitigating potential battery faults and failures.

articleTitle: An Experimental Demonstration of 2D-MIMO Based Deep Learning for OCC System
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: At present, radio frequency (RF) signals are extensively utilized across wireless communication systems, playing a pivotal role in enhancing various applications of human life. Particularly in Internet of Things (IoT) and Smart factory systems, wireless communication tehcnologies offer ease of installation and deployment compared to wired technologies, ushering in numerous benefits. Nonetheless, the higher frequencies of RF waves can make risks to human health. Consequently, researchers are exploring the visible light spectrum as a viable substitute to RF in wireless communication systems. Various approaches such as light fidelity (LiFi), visible light communication (VLC), and optical camera communication (OCC) have been investigated. This article introduces a novel technique utilizing LED matrix, employing time-domain on-off keying, suitabling for smart factory system. In this study, we proposed OCC architecture, which is adaptable and compatible with both the rolling shutter camera and the global shutter camera, such as webcam, smartphone, CCTV, etc. By applying Artificial Intelligence (AI) for LED detection, the proposed approach demonstrates superior performance compared to conventional methods. By controlling of shuttle speed, camera focal length, and applying the suitable channel coding, we can achieve two links at varying positions within an 7m communication range, considering mobility effects at 3 meters per second.

articleTitle: Exploring the Cinemaverse: Data-Driven Analysis of Movie Production, Revenue, and Trends Using Tableau Visualization Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Effective data visualization is essential for extracting meaningful insights from complex datasets in today's data-driven world. This paper showcases the power of data visualization by transforming the IMDB movies dataset into an interactive and informative dashboard using Tableau, a leading data visualization platform. The paper delves into the global distribution of movie releases, identifies the top-performing movie genres, examines the correlation between budget and box office success, highlights the most financially successful movies, and assesses the linguistic diversity of the dataset. The dashboard presented in the paper insights concisely through maps, treemaps, bar graphs, area charts, scatter plots, and pie charts. This paper also highlights the versatility of Tableau as a tool for creating interactive and visually appealing dashboards that a wide range of audiences can use.

articleTitle: Energy Surplus Power Trading and Sharing Service Platform for Housing Complexes
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: When energy management is performed by combining multiple households, it is possible to achieve positive energy using only PV and ESS of smaller capacity by using the difference in consumption patterns among houses. Energy independence can also be achieved through energy management through groups with multiple households, and profit from small-scale electricity sales of plus-energy.

articleTitle: Research on Digital Cultural Heritage Expansion Using AI Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Since the early 2000s, the digital transformation of the National Museum of Korea has led to the creation of numerous digital data related to artifacts. When the initial digital cultural heritage data began to be accumulated, the focus was on ‘recording’ rather than ‘public disclosure’, so the data disclosed to the public was extremely small. In addition, unlike systematically managed cultural heritage, ‘replicated data’ in digital form is relatively unstructured in terms of creation, management, and storage. To systematize the many digital data that are piled up in a disorderly manner, a lot of manpower and cost must be invested, but there are limits to solving this with limited resources. This study proposes a standard for classifying cultural heritage data by introducing artificial intelligence technology to solve these problems, and further suggests ways to use digital data more creatively using artificial intelligence technology.

articleTitle: A Word-axis Speaker Embedding Trained with Multi-Speaker Analysis Task
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In recent research, there has been an increased use of pre-trained speaker vectors as conditions for voice synthesis. While these are useful for speaker verification, they have intrinsic limitations in the range of information they cover, leading to a situation where the vocoder plays a critical role in learning and reconstructing formants. In this paper, we aim to extract time-variant speaker embeddings that are more conducive to speech synthesis and have a cognitively meaningful distribution. We propose and evaluate a method for extracting speaker embeddings along the word-axis, which is multi-task trained in a multi-speaker analysis context. Our method has shown improved performance over existing methods both in speaker verification tasks and in aligning with human perception.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition in Images and Video with Python For Autism Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The FER python library used in tandem with the OpenCV python library can be used to detect emotions in humans captured both in video and in images. The motivation of this work could be used to diagnose autism in people. FER is a library consisting of a CNN (convolutional neural network) for detecting emotions, and OpenCV is a library used for computer vision and machine learning. OpenCV is capable of producing impressive results involving facial recognition and tracking, meanwhile FER can see improvement in emotion recognition. One of the many signs of a young individual being on the autism spectrum is an inability to recognize emotions in the faces of others. Knowing this, this project has been designed to recognize emotions in people's faces, and test individuals on their emotion recognition skills in order to possibly aid in the diagnosis of autism.

articleTitle: Facial Expression Parameters Extraction Using Graph Convolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper addresses a deep learning framework for the extraction of Facial Action Coding System coefficients from 3D facial models. To optimize the labor-intensive process associated with facial animation using traditional Blendshapes, this framework employs a Graph Convolution Network to extract feature vectors from 3D facial models, and accurately infers expression coefficients based on the Facial Action Coding System.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation of Effect of FP on QoS Controls in IEEE 802.1TSN over In-Vehicle Networks by Multiple Regression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper studies the quantitative effect of Frame Preemption (FP) defined in IEEE 802.1 TSN, a standard for transmitting time-sensitive data on Ethernet when used with CBS and TAS, which are QoS controls in IEEE 802.1 TSN. Since FP is a method of preferentially transmitting highly urgent intermittent traffic, it is necessary for in-vehicle networks. When designing an in-vehicle network, it is essential to evaluate the effect of FP on other priority control methods. However, since it operates independently of other QoS controls, it isn't easy to estimate the effect of FP when combining it with other QoS controls. This paper uses an in-vehicle network QoS estimation based on multiple regression analysis to quantitatively evaluate the effectiveness of FP in an Ethernet-based in-vehicle network that combines CBS, TAS, and FP.

articleTitle: Simulation Design for Learning Data Collection to Estimate UAM Location in GNSS-Denied using 3D Spatial Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: We propose a simulation framework to collect training data that enhances urban air mobility location estimation in GNSS-denied environments. Leveraging a 3D engine to accurately replicate urban environments, the simulation uses tile indexing for spatial information management. We aim to provide training datasets that include visual information for visual odometry and spatial properties for spatial analysis. This encompasses not only building models and aerial photographs for realistic navigation scenes but also attributes essential for constructing spatial analysis data, including building bounding boxes, addresses, and intricate geometric details.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Channel Estimation Method Using Deep Learning for OFDM System
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In the time- and frequency-variant mobile radio channel such as the Fifth- and Forth-Generation mobile communications systems (5G, 4G), it is very important to estimate the channel coefficients (gains). We propose an estimation method of channel coefficients using a deep learning. The high accuracy of estimation can be evaluated using the deep learning method for super-resolution (SR) Network compared with the conventional method. The estimation of channel gains using orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) can be replaced with the SR problem and applied to the SR Network method. We show that the accuracy of the proposed method is higher than the conventional methods.

articleTitle: Medical Healthcare Digital Twin Reference Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The importance of effectively combining real-world data and virtual-world simulation functions through a digital twin-based solution platform is rapidly increasing. A reference platform to support this is strongly required. The mental healthcare management of emotional workers is a requirement area that has limitations in existing medical healthcare management because it is challenging to consider the emotional response at the time of a stressful situation and the individual's underlying state is not reflected. In this study, we construct a medical healthcare digital twin solution architecture for a personalized stress risk management solution and present an effective mental healthcare management method through each layer of technology. In the digital twin structure, for medical health risk management due to emotional labor, individual stress risks factors such as emotion/body reaction and environment are extracted with various modalities, and stress risk is precisely predicted through synchronization/modeling of dynamic objects in a virtual space. Generally, it provides a medical health care digital twin platform solution for personalized medical health risk prediction that can be configured according to the environment by providing an intervention tailored to the customer and can be improved according to the user's feedback.

articleTitle: Transmittance-Based Classification of Semiconductor Slit Designs: A Novel Multi-Layer Perceptron Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) classifier for classifying random and simple slit designs based on their transmittance values in semiconductor manufacturing processes. Experimental results demonstrate high accuracy in this classification task, presenting the stark difference in transmittance between the two design types. We also present the ratio of random and simple slit design data for optimal learning in data composition schemes. This approach offers potential cost reductions in data collection for machine learning model training, with implications for optimizing semiconductor processes. The study sheds light on the tangible association between transmittance values and design structures, suggesting potential complexity reductions in deep learning models for process optimization.

articleTitle: Implementation of Root Zone Management System Utilizing Predictive Modelling for Optimized Nutrient Solution Supply in Hydroponic Floriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This study explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and advanced sensors can improve flower farming, focusing on chrysanthemums and roses. A new type of sensor was developed to better measure electrical conductivity(EC) in water and used AI to predict how much water and nutrients the plants need. The results are promising for making floriculture farming more sustainable and productive, using less water and nutrients while maintaining high-quality plants. This approach could help floriculture farmers face the challenges of today's market, offering a step towards the future of farming with technology.

articleTitle: Proposal and Evaluation of a Hidden Terminal Identification Method Using Terminal-to-Terminal Information Exchange for Highly Sensitive Carrier Sensing in LPWAN
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Competitive access methods using carrier sense are used in LPWA-based wireless networks. Since the sensing detection range is finite, there is a problem of packet collision due to the inability to detect the signal being accessed. Identifying hidden terminals, which are terminals that cannot detect packet accesses, is effective in avoiding packet collisions. This study es-tablished a method to identify hidden terminals by evaluating the sensing performance of each terminal and sharing the evaluation results through inter-terminal communication. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by computer simulation.

articleTitle: A Performance Evaluation Method Based on Virtualization Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: With the iterative upgrading of communication protocols, the complexity of the communication systems is increasing rapidly. In order to satisfy the requirements of implementation complexity, the hardware of the user equipment (UE) has to be upgraded and replaced, resulting in a large amount of electronic wastes. However, the software defined radio (SDR) is designed based on softwares using a general hardware platform. Therefore, only the software upgrade is needed for the communication system if the UE is implemented by SDR. The resource waste can also be reduced greatly. In order to match the computational re-sources of the hardware platform to the computing requirements of the software implementation, a performance evaluation model is studied in this paper. A general scheme is proposed to estimate the computational complexity of the signal processing for the specific communication protocol. Then, the computational ability of the hardware platform can be evaluated compared with the estimated complexity to determine if the hardware can support the specific communication protocol. The numerical results of typical communication systems are also provided to assess the proposed model.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Two-Step Random Access for Low-Latency Communications in 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a two-step random access (RA) scheme in cellular systems, which is considered as one of essential techniques for enabling low-latency communications in 6G. We provide detailed description on the overall procedure of the two-step RA. Thereafter, we mathematically analyze its performance especially in terms of the one-shot success probability, the probability of success after fallback to the conventional 4-step RA, and the probability of failure after fallback to the 4-step RA. Through extensive simulations, we verify the validity of our numerical analysis, and investigate the effect of the primary control parameter (i.e., mapping coefficient between physical RA channel and physical uplink shared channel) on the overall performance of the two-step RA procedure.

articleTitle: Raspberry Pi with Real-Time Kernel
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The paper addresses the formidable challenge of processing large volumes of data generated by Lidar sensors in autonomous vehicles. Unlike compact MCUs, which may struggle to cope with the sheer magnitude of data flow from these sensors, the paper proposes an alternative solution involving the utilization of Raspberry Pi 3 equipped with a real-time kernel. This approach harnesses the computational power and versatility of the Raspberry Pi 3 to efficiently manage the influx of data from Lidar sensors while ensuring real-time responsiveness–a critical requirement for autonomous vehicle operations.

articleTitle: Using Multi-Scale Feature Predictions for FPN Architecture Based Real-Time Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Semantic segmentation is a challenging topic that requires the categorization of every pixel of input images. When each pixel output is computed by neighborhood values from the previous stage, the field of views is directly affected by feature extraction. A large receptive field captures many classes for a single shoot, so it leads to poor extraction. When a receptive field is small, it can not cover the global information of large objects. Feature pyramid network (FPN) includes multi-scale features to process information. Four features with different receptive views are suitable for extracting a long range of objective sizes. However, the feature aggregation of the FPN method is not optimal when it demands huge computation resources and reduces rich semantic information by concatenating all features together. In order to address the above limitations, this paper proposes multi-scale feature predictions based on the traditional FPN method to improve the model's performance and efficiency. The proposed decoder comprises two predictions to effectively process highlighted information from each feature. A pair of the feature pyramid is selected to generate one prediction. The context and spatial branches have different contributions to the progression of information-sharing. When the atrous spatial pyramid pooling is applied to the context path to obtain denser information, the spatial branch is basically processed by a convolution layer to maintain the coarse information. The model is trained and evaluated by different public datasets. We achieved outstanding results with 76.2 % mIoU and 65 FPS on Cityscapes, and 43.5 % mIoU on the Mapillary Vistas dataset.

articleTitle: A Moving Object Tracking in Video Sequences Using Finite Memory Structure Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, an alternative moving object tracking scheme in video sequences is proposed using the finite memory structure(FMS) filter. The proposed FMS filter based moving object tracking scheme provides estimates for position as well as acceleration of moving object in real-time video sequences, while eliminating unwanted noise effects and maintaining desired moving trajectory. Computer simulation results show that the performance of the FMS filter based scheme can be better than existing Kalman filter based scheme when the moving direction of the object in video sequences is suddenly changed.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Optimizers for YOLOv8n Based Smoker Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper introduces automatic labeling technology to overcome the time-consuming and high cost problems of the existing manual labeling process, with the aim to distinguish between smokers and non-smokers. To address this problem, we present an efficient data labelling method that utilizes computer vision to improve an object detection system for identifying smokers. We also present a comparative analysis of various optimizers - including SGD, Adam, AdamW, Nadam, and RAdam - focusing on their impact on the performance of the YOLOv8n model, which is used to detect smoking behavior. The comparative analysis reveals that the Adam optimizer achieves higher accuracy in detecting objects related to smoking behavior compared to others.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Multi-LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper proposes energy-efficient networking strategies for non-terrestrial communication systems where mul-tiple low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites support several ground access points (GAPs). Each LEO satellite exploits multiple spot beams to mitigate intra-LEO interference. Also, to manage inter-LEO interference, it is necessary to involve GAP-LEO scheduling optimization. We aim to design nested association policies among multiple LEO satellites, spot beams, and GAPs that can maximize the global energy efficiency (GEE) performance of multi-LEO satellite networks. To overcome the nondeterministic polynomial-time hard (NP-hard) nature of the original GEE maximization problem, we present a useful reformulation procedure and provide the optimal solution. The numerical results verify the effectiveness of our proposed solution in diverse system setups.

articleTitle: ARQ Delay in Underwater Acoustic Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The paper analyzes the delay of a go back <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> ARQ protocol across an underwater acoustic communication channel. The focus is on data transmission between a bottom mounted sensor node and an aggregation point. It is assumed that packets generated by the sensor node can be described by a Poisson process. The transmission queue is modeled as an M/G!1 queue. Numerical examples are presented that illustrate the ARQ delay performance for various distances between the transmitter and the receiver.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Task Splitting and Cell-Free MIMO Transmission for Multi-Tier Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Multi-tier computing employing computation of-floading to edge servers (ESs) or cloud servers (CSs) offers a solution for challenges for intensive tasks at mobile devices having limited computing resources. We tackle a joint design to minimize completion time, dividing tasks into subtasks processed by local servers, ESs, and CSs. We jointly optimize task splitting ratios and transmission strategies. Numerical results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed multi-tier computing systems.

articleTitle: Advancing Multi-Agent Systems Integrating Federated Learning with Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Recent advancements in the field of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), such as the development of algorithms like Deep Q-Network, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), have been significant. However, these algorithms encounter data privacy issues in multi-agent environments. This paper investigates the latest research trends in applying federated learning to address data privacy issues in multi-agent systems within deep reinforcement learning. It delves into various approaches for implementing federated learning in these systems, examines the challenges faced, and explores potential solutions to enhance privacy while maintaining or improving the performance of DRL algorithms in multi-agent setting.

articleTitle: Collision Prediction and Driving Safety Warning System for Mobile Robots Using 3D LiDAR and 2D Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The introduction of advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) is playing a pivotal role in modern vehicle technology, as advances in driver assistance technologies are key to improving road safety and driving comfort. This research detects and predicts far-field hazards that are beyond the range of traditional near-field radar-based systems. Here, we demonstrate a novel system that integrates 3D LiDAR and 2D camera technology to provide a comprehensive solution to these limitations. The system not only predicts potential collision points with high accuracy, but also provides advanced warning signals to the driver to improve reaction time and situational awareness. The results of the study show that this integrated approach successfully predicts far-field collision risk in a variety of scenarios, outperforming traditional radar-based ADAS. This research has important implications for the development of autonomous driving technology by showing how it can significantly reduce the incidence of traffic accidents and improve overall traffic safety. The implications of this research go beyond the immediate field and could influence future innovations in vehicle safety systems and help them evolve towards fully autonomous solutions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Low-Complexity Channel Impulse Response Estimation for Resource Management of Underwater Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based low-complexity channel impulse response (CIR) estimation method using a gated recurrent unit-convolutional neural network (GRU-CNN) based CIR estimator that estimates a CIR without feedback from a receiver. The proposed method estimates CIR using only SSP and seafloor information with low complexity using GRU and a one-dimensional convolutional layer. The simulation results show that the proposed method has the lowest mean squared error (MSE) of CIR estimation compared to other deep learning models and lower complexity than the BELLHOP estimator.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Sensing-Aided Beam Prediction using Poolformer for UAV Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a deep learning technique that uses both camera image data and GPS data to predict the optimal beam for efficient beamforming in UAV communication systems. Previous research has proposed single-modal beam prediction models that use either camera image data or GPS data individually. However, such methods have limitations due to their sensitivity to the measurement environment and outliers. To overcome this, we suggest a new technique based on Poolformer, a derivative model of the transformer, which combines these two types of data. Experimental results show that the proposed Poolformer-based model outperforms the existing model in terms of Top-1, 2, 3 accuracy for both 32 and 64 beams. Notably, the Top-3 accuracy of the proposed model approached nearly 100% accuracy in both experiments.

articleTitle: Horizontal Soft Handover Management in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Efficient system performance enhancement and reduction of signaling overhead in Cell-Free (CF) networks can be achieved through the strategic design of horizontal soft handover management. However, in a typical CF environment, Access Points (AP) are often collocated at short distances, posing challenges to the efficient design of horizontal soft handovers. Furthermore, utilizing traditional handover techniques in such scenarios can lead to improper handovers and incorrect AP selection. We propose a horizontal handover technique to help CF networks overcome these challenges. The proposed technique comprises three key components: 1) handover triggering, 2) AP selection, and 3) AP clustering. To minimize scanning delays, the handover triggering mechanism relies on sharing Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI) values among users. Additionally, AP selection and clustering are tailored based on the applications running on the Mobile Node (MN) device. The system is tested across AP distribution scenarios to assess handover delay, throughput, and packet loss. The performance evaluation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed system, particularly in dense AP environments with varying numbers of MNs.

articleTitle: A Research Trends of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for C-V2X Network Resource Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: An extension of the concept of IoT, The vehicle Internet of Things (IoV) can support smart city development. For smooth communication of vehicle communication, is core of IoV, various requirements such as coverage range, latency, and throughput must be satisfied. Cellular-based C-V2X has emerged to solve this problem. C-V2X requires Resource Allocation (RA) to solve dense and heterogeneous networks. Recently, many studies applying Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) have been carried out and their performance has been proven. This paper investigates trend of C-V2X communication Resource Allocation using reinforcement learning for intelligent Resource Allocation.

articleTitle: Scalable Emotion Recognition Model with Context Information for Driver Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: Understanding emotions from an individual's per-spective is critical for daily social interactions. If machines could similarly comprehend emotions, they could interact more effectively with people. Recognizing emotions accurately often necessitates considering the situational context, which helps in identifying a broader spectrum of emotions. Current emotion detection systems predominantly rely on facial images, often overlooking contextual influences. This paper proposes an emotion recognition model that combines facial feature analysis with an understanding of the surrounding context. The validation on the EMOTIC benchmark confirms the model's usefulness, registering an overall accuracy percentage of 84.9%. The paper emphasizes the necessity of combining contextual information for more accurate emotion recognition, which will pave the way for advances in sectors such as medical imaging, augmented reality, and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated System for Responding to Emergency Situations by Identifying Users' Lifelogs
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The widespread use of digital technology and mobile devices has led to the creation of lifelogs, which record users' daily activities, locations, and health statuses. These lifelogs can be crucial for enhancing emergency response services. Recognizing this potential, the Korean government has prioritized improving emergency medical services through initiatives like the Emergency Medical Basic Plan. However, current emergency response systems often overlook lifelogs and rely on traditional emergency call systems, missing the opportunity for personalized responses. This study proposes an integrated system that leverages lifelog data to enhance emergency services by monitoring lifelog data in real-time, swiftly identifying emergencies, and providing personalized services tailored to users' needs. The paper analyzes the current state of emergency response services and the potential of lifelog data, identifying key challenges. The proposed system includes features such as lifelogs based emergency recognition and prediction, personalized service provision, user notification, and situation reporting. By integrating lifelog data, the study aims to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of emergency medical services, enhancing user safety and convenience. This research highlights the importance of technological advancements in emergency response and advocates for continued innovation to develop more efficient and accurate systems in the future.

articleTitle: A Novel IoT Middleware for Secure Pharmaceuticals Condition Monitoring in Supply Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of blockchain technology and the Internet of Things (IoT) to enhance safety and traceability for the pharmaceutical supply chain, primarily focusing on medication storage. This research arises from challenges tied to improper warehousing procedures and the requirement for flawless data accuracy among various participants in the supply chain. In order to track and monitor the conditions of medical supplies, an IoT middleware is developed that utilises the Hyperledger Fabric Blockchain. The data gathered from IoT end-points is securely transmitted to the node running the HyperLedger Blockchain using the MQTT protocol. The developed prototype provides an immutable history of drug storage conditions, such as temperature, and humidity. To ascertain the system's performance, we have conducted systematic tests. The experimental results suggest that the developed proof of concept demonstrates its ability to handle different loads, maintain optimal transaction throughput and latency and efficiently manage and secure IoT data in real-time. Moreover, it ensures continuous data collection from supply chain IoT nodes and synchronisation with the blockchain network.

articleTitle: A study on throughput coverage evaluation of non-terrestrial communication base stations
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: In this paper, we assume a non-terrestrial communication base station that aims to improve population coverage and expand communication coverage in preparation for post-disaster scenarios. The transmission performance was numerically evaluated when changing altitude, adopted frequency band, etc. Additionally, appropriate altitudes and frequency bands will be discussed based on the evaluation results.

articleTitle: AirFogComp: Over-the-Air-Fog Computation for Federated Learning over Fog-RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This work studies an over-the-air-fog computation (AirFogComp) system, wherein Internet-of- Things (IoT) devices collaboratively learn a machine learning model by communicating with a central server (CS) through a network of access points (APs). Considering the finite capacity of fronthaul links between APs and the CS, we address the challenge of jointly optimizing linear precoding at the IDs, linear processing, and quantization noise covariance matrices at the APs, along with linear combining at the CS. The objective is to minimize the mean squared error (MSE) of the target vector, which is defined as a weighted sum of the local model vectors. To tackle this optimization problem, we propose an iterative block coordinated descent (BCD) algorithm. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid convergence of the proposed algorithm and its superior performance compared to baseline schemes.

articleTitle: Design of Horticultural Therapy Content in Virtual Reality Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: This study aims to design greenhouse management content in a virtual reality environment to provide users with mental care and psychological stability. In the implemented virtual reality, users can feel psychological stability and a sense of achievement by freely placing the plants they want and managing the greenhouse using controllers. Additionally, the use of already marketed game engines and Head Mounted Display for this content facilitates future improvements and additions, and it is designed to accommodate a diverse range of users. Plans are in place to enhance user experience through further research and consultation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Drone Communication Utilizing 4QAM OFDM in OCC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Fifteenth International Conference on Ubiquitous and Future Networks (ICUFN)
abstract: The advantages and potential applications of drones are increasingly sought after, particularly in the field of communication.
